The `android14-*.txt` notification fixtures were captured on 2026-11-20 from Android 14 in the isolated LDPlayer `CareerPilotValidation` instance 1, serial `emulator-5556`.

The notification source was a separate fictional app, `app.careerpilot.callfixture`. It used Android's native `Notification.CallStyle` incoming, ongoing and screening constructors, `MessagingStyle`, `BigTextStyle` with `CATEGORY_MISSED_CALL`, and a call group summary. No audio, network, caller data or Hushed account was used. Hushed was not installed in that validation instance. Only notification framing, flags and typed template/call-type metadata remain; titles, text, person values, actions and intents were discarded. The transient record identity and fixture UID were normalized.

`android14-production-filter.txt` was obtained while the fictional incoming notification existed, using the actual production command's `--package com.hushed.release`. It contains no notification records, proving that the separate fixture is excluded. Unit tests first assert that every unmodified fixture is rejected by the production package check, then normalize the package **inside tests only** to exercise native metadata parsing.

This is framework-format and package-isolation evidence. It does not establish that the real Hushed app emits these signals or verify any actual Hushed call. The initial fixture exposed Android's requirement that CallStyle notifications have a foreground service or full-screen intent; the fixture subsequently used a no-op full-screen intent and all six notification states plus cancellation were captured successfully.

Raw notification dumps were not retained. The fixture APK and build/collection scripts are local ignored validation artifacts in `.implementation/hushed-call-fixture/`.

`telecom-android14-registered-idle.txt` and `telecom-android14-empty.txt` contain actual sanitized Telecom output from the same isolated emulator. The separate fictional app `app.careerpilot.telecomfixture` registered a self-managed PhoneAccount. Current `mCalls` was empty both while its account was registered and after it was cleared. The recapture used registration-only mode and attempted no incoming call. Native section boundaries, the account formatter, enabled flags, service components, capabilities, routes and URI schemes are preserved, including the existing Android system telephony account. Account and group identifiers were replaced with `***FIXTURE***`; non-null account extras were replaced with `[REDACTED]`. Unused subsection contents, handles, callers, logs and historical events were discarded. The native `test emergency PhoneAccount filter: null` and `Analytics:` boundaries remain so parsers can verify the sections are complete. Registration alone is not evidence of a call.

Native Telecom lifecycle validation was blocked by this LDPlayer image's service-binding behavior. The installed compiled manifest had an exported service, `android.permission.BIND_TELECOM_CONNECTION_SERVICE`, and the correct `android.telecom.ConnectionService` intent action. The fixture's account permitted incoming calls and its service could start. In the same APK, binding to that explicit component without an action succeeded, binding with a separate fixture action succeeded, and binding with the standard Telecom action returned false. Telecom therefore failed before invoking the ConnectionService incoming-call callback; no native ringing, active, held or disconnected call row was captured. This observation does not establish the cause of the emulator behavior or prove how the real Hushed app behaves.

`telecom-synthetic-*.txt` are explicitly hand-authored parser inputs based on the [Android 14 Call serialization contract](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/services/Telecomm/+/android-14.0.0_r1/src/com/android/server/telecom/Call.java). They are **not captured native output**. They contain the complete source-based call/account field order and section boundaries, with `***SYNTHETIC***` placeholders for account and handle values. Tests may normalize the component to Hushed only inside the test; the unmodified files must be excluded by the production ownership check. Positive native lifecycle validation remains outstanding.

The local ignored Telecom fixture source, diagnostic modes, build script and idle-only collector are in `.implementation/hushed-telecom-fixture/`. The binding-diagnostic APK's SHA-256 was `f1a32f129c0a1de4ef54054baa47309e3a1001cf3cafc66329145e371eb964c3`; the subsequent registration-only recapture APK is `67250502eddec02cebf98da2af043a5be70b5546cc71ffc2ab2f632455029065`. The fixture requested no microphone or network permission, started no media stream, and placed no real call. Its account, service, app and isolated emulator were cleaned up after validation; the user's instance 0 was not changed.
